description:
Redwood Inference is running a Reliability Program focused on reducing incident frequency and improving MTTR via clearer ownership, consistent classification, and better tooling. This project—"Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping"—defines a standardized incident taxonomy (top incident types and subtypes), maps each type to a primary owning team/service, and establishes remediation SLAs (time-to-mitigate and time-to-fix expectations) by severity/tier (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

Goals:
- Produce a v1 incident taxonomy that is easy for on-call engineers to apply during live incidents and consistent enough for reporting.
- Map each incident type to a single primary owner (with secondary/consulted teams) and define escalation rules.
- Define remediation SLAs per incident type and severity, aligned with customer commitments and internal SLO/error budget policy.
- Integrate taxonomy + ownership into incident tooling (incident-bot, postmortem templates, dashboards, alerts) so classification is required, auditable, and measurable.
- Create reporting that shows incident volume, impact, and SLA compliance by type/owner to drive incident reduction work.

Scope:
- In-scope incident classes: availability (5xx/overload), latency regressions, streaming disconnects, routing/fallback misbehavior, capacity/fleet shortages, control plane outages, auth/RBAC failures, telemetry/metrics blind spots, and private deployment connectivity/config issues.
- Includes both customer-impacting incidents and high-severity internal incidents that threaten reliability.
- Out-of-scope for v1: deep root-cause frameworks (kept in postmortems), long-term product roadmap changes not tied to incident reduction.

Stakeholders and teams:
- Core: SRE (program lead, standards, dashboards), Platform Control Plane + Smart Routing (ownership mapping for routing/config), Infra/Fleet (capacity- and region-related types), Observability (metrics/cardinality/dashboards), Serving Runtime (runtime regression types), Security Ops (security incident alignment), Support/CS (customer comms + escalation mapping), Product (alignment with SLA commitments and Console surfacing).

Phases and timeline (typical 6–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + data pull: analyze recent incidents and support escalations; propose top 10–15 categories.
2) Taxonomy workshop(s): converge on definitions, decision tree, and examples.
3) Ownership + SLA alignment: validate owners with EMs/Directors; align remediation SLAs with customer tiers and incident process.
4) Tooling integration: incident-bot required fields, control-plane config for owner mapping, metrics labels, dashboards/alerts, and postmortem template updates.
5) Rollout + training: on-call playbook updates, announcements, office hours; enforce required classification; measure compliance.

Key constraints:
- Keep taxonomy low-cardinality and stable (avoid exploding label cardinality in metrics).
- Owners must be accountable and match real operational control boundaries.
- Remediation SLAs must be realistic given fleet constraints and release processes, while still driving meaningful improvement.

Primary deliverables:
- Confluence: published taxonomy definitions + decision tree, ownership mapping table, remediation SLA matrix, incident-process policy updates, ADR.
- Linear: implementation and rollout work items with dependencies.
- GitHub: PRs across incident-bot, redwood (instrumentation/control plane), observability-pack, slo-toolkit, docs.
- Slack: decision threads, rollout comms, live incident classification examples.
- Drive: working spreadsheets/analysis and workshop notes.
- Jira: representative support tickets linked back to taxonomy categories for validation.
- Fireflies: workshop transcript and select customer post-incident reviews used to validate comms + SLA alignment.
